items.text: The process that loads this table has not been found anywhere in the available material. The table combines data from 9 different partner sources: 5 are still active and updated today (WEIS Earn, AMS POS, WEIS GAS N GO, SUNOCO Redeem, MIRABITO Redeem), and 4 stopped receiving data years ago (SHEETZ Redeem and HIGHS Redeem and CARROLLMF Redeem since late 2021, plus a tiny group since 2023)

SUNOCO Redeem is the same Sunoco fuel rewards partnership already seen on SUNOCO_FUEL_PRTNR_PRGM_F; MIRABITO is another active gas station chain partner. SHEETZ, HIGHS and CARROLLMF are the same type of partner but have not contributed points in about five years

One file found during the review is a monitoring report, not a loader: it reads this table to track how many records arrive from each partner source each day, confirming that freshness monitoring by source is already a standard practice at Weis

3 unrelated files carry a leftover header comment claiming to affect this table, but their actual content is unrelated general ledger work with nothing touching this table: a mislabeled template comment, the same pattern already seen elsewhere in this project
A duplicate staging table exists alongside the live one but holds no data and has never been used: a dead, unused copy, not a second active pipeline
No invalid internal keys were found across all 479,315,724 rows. The full business key was not checked for duplicates, to avoid an expensive scan

blocks.text: Still open, not confirmed in code or data yet. None of this blocks the lineage above, it is tracked here so nothing gets forgotten.

items.text: The system or process that actually loads this table has not been identified. It is clearly active, receiving data from 5 real partner sources, but nothing in the available material shows how
items.note: This is a 479 million row table central to fuel rewards partnerships; knowing how it is loaded matters directly for planning the migration

items.text: Whether the SHEETZ, HIGHS and CARROLLMF fuel rewards partnerships formally ended around late 2021, or their feeds simply broke, is unconfirmed
items.note: This affects whether the migration needs to plan for these sources coming back, or whether they can be treated as permanently retired

blocks.text: A few things below are still not fully confirmed. We are sharing this table's analysis now rather than holding it back, because the rest of it is solid and these gaps are clearly called out here, not hidden.

items.text: Still unknown: who gets notified if this process fails.
items.note: A real failure-alert file exists, naming 3 Weis staff, but we could not find what triggers it, so we cannot confirm it is actually wired into this table's live pipeline.

items.text: Still unknown: whether this process runs on a set schedule.
items.note: We could not find the program that loads this table anywhere in the files we have, so we have no way to confirm how often it runs.
